Two California Highway Patrol officers are recovering from serious injuries after a Tesla drove into their patrol car at a crash scene on Interstate 80 in Fairfield. The 22-year-old driver told investigators he was asleep with Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving” engaged.
CHP released dashcam video of the impact on Thursday. It’s the latest Tesla to plow into an emergency scene, a failure federal regulators started investigating five years ago.
Flares, cones, and four closed lanes
The crash happened just before midnight on Tuesday, October 13, on eastbound I-80 west of Air Base Parkway. Officers were there for an earlier fatal crash: about an hour before, a 19-year-old from San Pablo lost control of his Honda Civic and was hit by a Chevrolet Tahoe. He didn’t survive.
Four lanes were already shut down behind flares and cones when the Tesla showed up at freeway speed, per CHP. It went through the closure and into a Dodge Charger patrol car with both officers sitting in it. Cameras on the Charger and on another vehicle at the scene caught the impact.

The Tesla driver, from Sacramento, walked away with minor injuries. Both crashes are still under investigation.
In its statement, CHP stressed that FSD is a driver-assistance feature that requires the person behind the wheel to stay alert and in control: “Technology does not relieve drivers of their responsibility to safely operate their vehicles.”
CHP hasn’t released the Tesla model or the software version. And for now, the driver’s word is the only evidence FSD was on. Tesla’s vehicle logs will settle that.
Five years of Teslas hitting emergency scenes
We’ve been here before. In August 2021, NHTSA opened an investigation after a series of Teslas on Autopilot crashed into stopped police cars and fire trucks , many of them at night with flares, cones, and flashing lights on scene. That probe ended with Tesla’s December 2023 recall of more than 2 million vehicles, fixed with an over-the-air update that added more driver-attention alerts.
FSD hasn’t solved it either. In June 2024, a Tesla on FSD hit a parked Fullerton police car while officers were handling, again, a fatal crash. That driver admitted to being on his phone.
A nighttime lane closure lit up with flares is about as clear a “stop or move over” signal as a road can give. If FSD was engaged in Fairfield, it drove straight into one at highway speed.
The driver monitoring problem
FSD (Supervised) uses the cabin camera to make sure the driver is watching the road. It’s supposed to nag, then disengage, when someone isn’t paying attention. A driver who’s actually asleep shouldn’t get very far.
So either he hadn’t been asleep for long, or the camera didn’t catch it. We don’t know which yet. But Tesla has been relaxing that monitoring, not tightening it. We recently reported that Tesla drivers can easily bypass the monitoring system , even a simple dollar bill placed in front of the camera can nullify it.
Last December, Elon Musk claimed FSD drivers can now text and drive “depending on context of surrounding traffic.” Texting while driving is illegal in California.
Electrek’s Take
The driver is responsible. If he fell asleep at the wheel at freeway speed, he nearly killed two cops who were already cleaning up after a fatal crash, and he should face the consequences. CHP is right about that.
But as usual, I have to emphasize Tesla’s responsibility here. Tesla doesn’t get to wash its hands of this. It sells a product called “Full Self-Driving” in the US, it agreed to drop that name in Europe this month after German regulators called it misleading, and its CEO tells owners they can text with it. When you tell people the car drives itself, some of them believe you. A 22-year-old driving home at midnight is exactly who believes you.
It’s the complacency issue I have been talking about for years. FSD gets more dangerous as it gets better. You go on social media and there are legions of Tesla fans who believe that the system is reliable for this. It clearly isn’t.
Juries are starting to see it that way too. Florida’s $243 million Autopilot verdict put a third of the blame on Tesla, and the Katy, Texas FSD crash earlier this year showed the same complacency trap from another angle. Driver fault and Tesla fault aren’t mutually exclusive.
And there’s the technical failure. Emergency scenes are the exact scenario NHTSA flagged in 2021. Five years and a 2-million-vehicle recall later, a Tesla on Tesla’s most advanced driver-assist software allegedly drove into one anyway. Musk keeps promising unsupervised FSD on customer cars. If Tesla wants to take the driver out of the loop, will it take the liability for crashes like this one? Until it does, it shouldn’t be telling anyone it’s OK to look away.

The American Trucking Associations wrapped up a busy week Friday as it prepares for its annual conference beginning Sunday, with the American Transportation Research Institute, ATA’s not-for-profit research organization, naming a new head the day after ATA announced a new chief of the entire organization.
Page Siplon will head up ATRI, according to a Friday announcement. He will hold the positions of president and chief operating officer.
According to ATRI, Siplon was most recently the CEO of TeamOne Logistics , a firm that partners with companies to provide drivers and other employees to carriers. “His leadership focused extensively on the trucking workforce, driver recruitment and retention, safety, and the operational challenges facing motor carriers,” ATRI said in its announcement of Siplon’s hiring.
The news of Siplon’s appointment comes a day after the ATA said it had hired Mark Colson, current head of the Alabama Trucking Association, to head the national organization.
Georgia background
TeamOne is based in Georgia, and Siplon’s career in logistics prior to that was focused on the Peach State.
Previously, Siplon had been executive director of the Georgia Center of Innovation for Logistics. He also founded the Georgia Logistics Summit, which ATRI described as “one of the nation’s largest logistics conferences.”
Siplon also has been vice chairman of the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Advisory Committee on Supply Chain Competitiveness.
Siplon will join the ATRI staff next month. He will work alongside current ATRI president Rebecca Brewster , who is retiring in February 2027. He will then assume his duties at the top of the organization.
Siplon’s announcement comes right before the ATA MCE meeting next week which also is when ATRI announces the results of its Top 10 survey. The input from that research into the top 10 issues separates the results out by totals and separate subcategories drawn from driver and management input, the latter of which often reveal a significantly different perspective between the two.
ATRI regularly conducts such surveys throughout the year. Earlier this week it announced two new surveys, one aimed at carriers and the other at drivers, on the issue of driver health.
Looking at driver health
The survey, according to ATRI, will take different approaches in its methodology.
ATRI said it would ask drivers to share anonymously several inputs, “as well as their experience with maintaining health and wellness while on the road.”
Carriers would be asked by ATRI for information on their fleets’ medical card durations, insurance costs and other key performance indicators. “Motor carriers are also strongly encouraged to share the driver survey with their driver workforce,” ATI said.
A medical card is more formally referred to as a Medical Examiner’s Certificate. It certifies a driver’s fitness to be on the road and is required by federal law.
In the prepared statement kicking off the health study, ATRI quoted Project 61 Founder & CEO Jeremy Reymer. ““We already know driver health can affect safety,” he said. “The next question is how much it may also be affecting operational risk and cost.”

Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe (PEJ) has commissioned Westinghouse Electric Co. to begin procuring long-lead items (LLIs) for the first AP1000 unit of the Lubiatowo-Kopalino nuclear power plant project. This is one of the most important stages in preparing for the start of construction and ensuring that the project is completed on schedule.
“This is an extremely important moment for the entire project. Securing long-lead items is of direct significance for the construction schedule of Poland’s first nuclear power plant. We want energy from the first reactor to reach our power outlets in 2036. This is a strategic project by the Polish government that will meet our needs for decades to come, becoming one of the cornerstones of our country’s energy security,” said Miłosz Motyka, Poland’s minister of Energy, in an October 8 news release.
“Thanks to the agreement reached in September between PEJ and the Consortium on the main commercial terms of the EPC contract, we are now ready to take the next step, namely begin the process of ordering long-lead items. We adopted this approach in order to give ourselves time for further detailed negotiations on the EPC contract, without the pressure that the lack of an LLI order would affect the project schedule. A sound contract that appropriately balances liability and establishes cooperation mechanisms for the construction phase is key to the project’s future success,” said Wojciech Wrochna, Secretary of State at the Ministry of Energy and the Government Plenipotentiary for Strategic Energy Infrastructure.
The scope of orders covers six key components of the nuclear island, including the reactor containment vessel and its associated structural modules. LLIs are among the most technologically advanced and complex components of a nuclear power plant, the production and delivery of which requires many years and the involvement of specialized suppliers that meet the highest quality and safety standards.
“In nuclear projects, proper preparation and effective time management are crucial. We have already ordered the first long-lead items for which Bechtel is responsible, and we are now beginning this process for Westinghouse, which is responsible for the nuclear portion of the power plant in the broadest sense. In this way, we safeguard not only the project schedule but also its budget. The components we order account for a significant part of our costs, so starting the process well in advance allows us to better control our expenses in the coming years,” said Marek Woszczyk, president of the Management Board of Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe.
Beginning the procurement process of long-lead items early is a common practice in nuclear projects around the world. It helps ensure the availability of production capacity, minimizes the risk of delays and supports the timely completion of projects. The scope of work includes preparing technical documentation, quality and supervision plans, selecting and contracting suppliers, as well as placing orders for the materials needed to begin production. The production and delivery of finished components to the construction site will be carried out as part of a subsequent order that PEJ plans to issue under the contract for the construction of the power plant.
“The ordering of long-lead items is a key milestone for this important project and helps to ensure it remains on schedule. Even more importantly, this is a critical first step for Polish industry to furnish nuclear-grade components for the plant and maximize its participation in Poland and in future AP1000 projects in Europe,” said Dan Lipman, president of Global Business Initiatives, Westinghouse.
The initiation of the procurement process for components with long-lead times is part of the current Engineering Development Agreement between PEJ and the Westinghouse-Bechtel consortium. PEJ and Westinghouse expect that Polish companies will bid for the contracts, provided they successfully complete the process of obtaining the ASME NQA-1 international quality standard. The high safety standards in the nuclear industry require that companies involved in the most specialized work meet stringent technical and quality requirements. This will be another step toward building domestic capabilities and create additional export opportunities for Polish industry to enter the global AP1000 technology supply chain.
The procurement of components with long-lead times is a crucial step in the preparations for the construction of Poland’s first nuclear power plant. The commissioning of the first unit at the Lubiatowo-Kopalino site is scheduled for 2036. The project will be one of the cornerstones of the national energy system, providing a stable, zero-emission source of energy for Poland.
—This content was contributed by Westinghouse .

A model of Zone 5's Eclipse drone interceptor on display at the 2026 AUSA conference. (Michael Marrow/Breaking Defense)
WASHINGTON — Defense startup Zone 5 is joining the rush for counter-drone tech, debuting a new interceptor dubbed the “Eclipse” that the company says can combat high-speed, unmanned threats.
Still in development but shown publicly for the first time at the Association of the United States Army conference here, the Eclipse offers a lower-cost, reusable option to take down high-speed drones, Zone 5 CEO Thomas Akers told Breaking Defense.
Arguing that the market is “coalescing” around smaller interceptors that are in turn challenged by more capable drones, Akers said his firm “found a spot” for a larger interceptor with modular payloads.
Larger doesn’t mean too large — an Eclipse model on display at Zone 5’s booth measured 39 in. long and 32 in. wide. But according to Akers, the platform can sport a high-powered microwave that can zap a drone’s electronics, or can carry a kinetic payload to knock one out of the sky. A company fact sheet said the Eclipse can take off and land vertically, achieve speeds of over 200 knots (230 miles per hour) and reach over 30 miles.
Akers said he expects Eclipse to be in development for roughly another six months before entering production, and is initially aimed at the American market. He said the company is aiming to build hundreds of copies a month but declined to comment on an expected price tag, pointing to various potential payloads that influence a final cost.
Akers explained that the Eclipse helps round out Zone 5’s offerings for layered defenses, from a drone-mounted firearm featured on the firm’s Paladin system to its White Spike anti-air missile. Zone 5’s burgeoning portfolio, which includes a cruise missile dubbed Rusty Dagger exported to Ukraine and on order for the Pentagon , likely helped attract the attention of the Norwegian defense firm Kongsberg, which completed an acquisition of Zone 5 earlier this year.
The Kongsberg acquisition “bring[s] kind of an immediate step change” regarding Zone 5’s access to international resources, Akers said. While Zone 5 still operates separately from Kongsberg in the United States, “globally, we present one unified front under the Kongsberg brand.”
The company’s new Norwegian ownership also “gives us access to a larger portfolio of vendors” that can help expand supply chains beyond the US, Akers added. Looking ahead, he said that the firm is going to remain focused on producing low-cost cruise missiles and technologies that can defeat Group 1-4 drones. A key goal is producing thousands of missiles annually, he said, along with leveraging Kongsberg resources to iterate on Zone 5’s products to increase lethality and survivability.
Alongside recent agreements like a Navy program for maritime strike and a Pentagon-wide effort for containerized munitions , one big opportunity for Zone 5, the Air Force’s Family of Affordable Mass Missiles (FAMM) program, is just over the horizon. In the coming years the service plans to acquire tens of thousands of FAMM missiles using multi-year deals, drawing from a pool of vendors including Zone 5, Anduril and CoAspire.
But after using dollars from the One Big Beautiful Bill to kickstart procurement in fiscal 2026, the Air Force once again banked on reconciliation to deliver funds for buying FAMM in FY27 — a prospect dimmed by doubts over another reconciliation bill.
“If multi-year doesn’t happen the way that it’s scheduled to, that sends a clear signal to industry,” Akers said, adding that a shortfall of appropriations means “you’re going to have, definitely, a recoil, and it’s going to be felt beyond just FAMM.”

source_document.body:
Carrier Logistics and LSP44 have partnered to develop an AI-powered API that can identify less-than-truckload shipments when a shipper or third-party logistics provider does not have the correct tracking number, targeting a source of manual work for carrier customer service teams.
The collaboration combines Carrier Logistics freight management software for LTL carriers with LSP44’s AI agent and API infrastructure for logistics service providers. The jointly developed technology allows shippers and 3PLs to submit other shipment details, including company names, delivery locations, shipment descriptions and approximate dates to search for freight through an automated connection.
“We’ve opened up the API to accept not just a pro number, but description of the shipment, an approximate date, where it’s getting delivered, and the names of the parties,” Carrier Logistics President Ben Wiesen said.
The companies announced the collaboration at Carrier Logistics’ user group conference in Chicago on Friday, Oct. 9. The partnership is now live, according to Carrier Logistics.
Traditional tracking APIs rely on a valid PRO number, the identifier used to track less-than-truckload shipments. When a shipper or broker doesn’t have the correct number, the carrier’s system may be unable to find the shipment, forcing the customer to call or email the carrier so an employee can locate the freight manually.
As more logistics companies automate communications, failed tracking requests can add to the volume of calls carriers must handle. LSP44 cited RXO ‘s report that its AI agents automated more than 500,000 phone calls in the first quarter of 2026, illustrating the growing scale of AI-driven communications in logistics. Also, at Carrier Logistics’ user conference on Friday, Oct. 9, Jeremy Estep, head of sales at LSP44 cited estimates that responding to bot communications can cost motor carriers upward of $10 per shipment.
“The industry has treated manual tracking requests as the cost of doing business for decades. Every carrier running LTL has a customer service team absorbing that cost today,” said Nick Ruggiero, LSP44’s head of product.
Wiesen described the problem from a carrier perspective.
“If both parties don’t know what the tracking number is, then that electronic communication fails,” Wiesen said.
The API searches recent shipment records and ranks potential matches using details such as origin and destination, ZIP codes, company names and other shipment characteristics. Shippers and 3PLs can compare the results with their own records to identify the correct shipment and resume electronic tracking.
The API first identifies potential shipment matches using defined search criteria. Carrier Logistics said AI then ranks those candidates by accounting for discrepancies in the available information. For example, it might recognize a shipment number with two incorrectly transcribed digits as a potential match, or rank a shipment higher when its ZIP code matches even if its listed weight differs from the search information.
Wiesen said the system searches around a week’s worth of shipment records. The approach is intended to replicate the work a customer service representative would perform when trying to identify freight from incomplete information.
The API is password-protected and uses account-specific credentials. Carrier Logistics said it considers only shipments associated with validated accounts as potential matches, limiting the records available through a search.
Testing whether the API reduces manual inquiries
The collaboration targets a specific failure point in freight automation: tracking requests that cannot be resolved because the requesting system lacks a valid shipment identifier.
Rather than deploying additional AI agents to respond to calls and emails generated by failed tracking requests, Carrier Logistics and LSP44 are attempting to resolve the identification problem at the API level.
“We could put voice bots on our side to answer voice bots on your side, and email-responding AI to email it. But why? Why can’t we just solve the bottleneck and the fundamental problem?” Wiesen said.
The system’s effectiveness will depend on whether it can identify the correct shipment from incomplete information and whether the requesting company’s software can use the results to resolve the inquiry without additional manual work.
The companies did not disclose how many carriers or customers would participate in the rollout.
“We can’t be sure it’s going to stop all the phone calls until we implement and deploy it,” Wiesen said.
LTL industry works toward standardized visibility
The partnership comes as the LTL industry develops common standards for exchanging shipment information across transportation systems.
The National Motor Freight Traffic Association’s Digital Standards Development Council has published an In-Transit Visibility API standard covering shipment status, delays and delivery estimates. The standard defines common milestones, including pickup, in transit, out for delivery and delivered, so shippers and logistics providers can interpret status updates consistently across carriers.
The council’s framework also provides for authenticated access to detailed shipment information and public access to certain status information. Its stated goal is to reduce reliance on phone calls and inconsistent tracking portals.
Carrier Logistics and LSP44 are addressing a related but distinct problem. Standardized data formats help systems communicate, but the new collaboration is designed to identify the shipment itself when the tracking number supplied in a request is missing or inaccurate.
That distinction matters for companies managing freight across multiple carriers and technology platforms. A system can successfully send an API request yet fail to retrieve the intended shipment if it cannot match the available information.
The API’s impact will depend on how accurately it identifies shipments from incomplete information and whether those matches reduce manual tracking inquiries. The companies have not yet established how many carriers or customers will participate in the rollout or how much manual work the system can eliminate.
Why this matters
As logistics companies automate more communications, missing or incorrect shipment identifiers can prevent tracking systems from finding freight and push inquiries back to carrier customer service teams. Carrier Logistics and LSP44 are trying to address that problem at the API level, rather than adding more automation to handle calls and emails. Whether the technology can reduce manual work will depend on its ability to match shipments accurately and its adoption by carriers and logistics providers.

Volkswagen is set to recall “several thousand” electric vehicles, including the ID.4 and ID. Buzz. The company is urging owners to limit charging to 80% until a fix is available.
Which EVs are included in the Volkswagen recall?
After recalling close to 100,000 electric vehicles globally earlier this year, Volkswagen is preparing for another major recall.
A company spokesperson told the German newspaper Handelsblatt that “several thousand” Volkswagen EVs are affected.
The recall follows an internal quality check that found some high-voltage battery cells do not meet quality requirements. According to the report, the affected models include the ID.3, ID.4, ID.7, and ID. Buzz, plus the Cupra Born, produced between 2023 and 2026.

Volkswagen already issued a recall with the NHTSA earlier this month, affecting 22,524 ID.4 SUVs for model years 2023 to 2026.
Until a fix is available, the company is urging owners to limit charging to 80% battery capacity. The root cause is still unknown, but VW said charging the high-voltage battery to over 80% in certain models could trigger “thermal propagation,” or a fire within the battery.
2025 Volkswagen Id.4 (Source: Volkswagen)
The company said the recall follows another field study as part of an ongoing review of Volkswagen vehicles not included in previous battery recall campaigns.
Volkswagen Group’s Product Safety Committee has requested “additional clarifications” from battery cell supplier SK Battery America about specific production dates and a potential clean date.
In the US, Volkswagen said it had received 22 claims between January 18, 2024, and August 07, 2026.
2025 Volkswagen ID.4 (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen is still working on a remedy. Notification letters warning owners of the safety risks are expected to be mailed out on November 27, 2026. Volkswagen will send additional letters once a fix is available.
In the meantime, owners can contact Volkswagen’s customer service at 1-800-893-5298 with any questions or concerns. VW’s recall number is 93EX.
Volkswagen has also issued a recall in the UK. The full details for the recall in Germany have yet to be listed by the German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA). Check back for updates, as this is a breaking development.

Buffalo Potash’s horizontal line-drive method uses parallel horizontal wells to circulate brine saturated with sodium chloride through potash-bearing rock. Credit: Buffalo Potash
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 16, 2026
Buffalo Potash (TSXV: BUFF; US-OTC: BLPTF) has secured Saskatchewan approval to complete construction and operate its first Disley potash facility, with first production still targeted for early 2027.
The initial production module, or IPM, about 50 km northwest of Regina, is designed to produce 125,000 tonnes annually. An April preliminary economic assessment estimated its capital cost at $29.2 million (C$41.5 million), including contingency.
“With our drilling program and completions program complete and equipping underway, this approval allows us to advance surface construction at the IPM site in parallel with our preparations for phase three of our development plan: brine circulation,” President and Chief Operating Officer Quinton Hardage said in a Friday news release.
The module is Buffalo’s commercial test of a patented mining method it hopes to expand into a much larger operation. The company intends to use early production to generate revenue and operating data for a feasibility study of two additional facilities. Financing and demonstrating that the method works commercially remain key tests.
Shares rose 2.6% to C80¢ by late Friday morning in Toronto, valuing Buffalo at about C$87.7 million. They’ve traded between C25¢ and C$1.07 over the past year.
Process innovation
Buffalo’s horizontal line-drive method uses parallel horizontal wells to circulate brine saturated with sodium chloride through potash-bearing rock. The brine selectively dissolves potassium chloride underground and carries it to the surface for processing into potash, used primarily in fertilizer.
The company has completed its source and disposal wells and horizontal drilling. Site development is underway, while brine circulation and installation of surface processing equipment remain steps toward startup, according to the release.
Buffalo plans to sell the initial facility’s soluble-grade potash locally for agricultural uses and as a drilling-fluid additive, according to its July update . The company intends to build local sales before the proposed larger facilities begin producing granular fertilizer for broader distribution. The April study also envisages producing potassium-chloride brine for regional oilfield customers.
Funding needs
Buffalo reported C$15.1 million in cash at June 30, following a C$14.85-million private placement. Its financial filing , dated Aug. 28, said it would need additional financing to advance Disley through a production decision and meet other commitments. Friday’s announcement didn’t provide an updated cash balance or remaining funding requirement.
The company is proceeding with the initial module without a feasibility study establishing mineral reserves and demonstrating economic and technical viability. Buffalo cautions that such production decisions carry a higher risk of economic and technical failure.
The provincial approval follows a Sept. 17 determination that the initial module didn’t require an environmental impact assessment. Conditions include approval of a site characterization and groundwater monitoring plan, meeting air-quality requirements before processing equipment operates and maintaining financial assurance acceptable to the ministry.
The permit runs until April 30, with provision for an extension. It covers only the initial module.
Expansion plans
Buffalo’s longer-term plan adds Disley East and Disley West, each designed to produce 500,000 tonnes annually, lifting combined capacity to about 1.13 million tonnes. The preliminary assessment estimated capital costs of $639 million across all three facilities.
That study assumed average prices of $374 per tonne for soluble-grade potash and $394 for granular product over its 25-year economic evaluation.
The larger facilities would require separate regulatory approvals and positive construction decisions following a feasibility study. Buffalo’s August financial filing said granular potash production and sales weren’t expected before 2029.

Stellantis Japan Rolls Out 2027 Jeep Avenger 4xe Hybrid Edition X, Only 170 Units Available
24 photos
Photo: Jeep
Precisely 170 copies of the Avenger 4xe Hybrid Edition X will be produced exclusively for the Japanese market. As per Stellantis Japan, the suggested retail price is 5,240,000 yen, tax included, regardless of paint finish. The limited-run model is nothing more than a styling-and-comfort affair with a bit of corporate poetry as the finishing touch.
X is the corporate poetry in question, with Stellantis Japan claiming that X stands for City x Outdoor, Weekday x Weekend, and Style x Capability. To peeps who can understand marketing talk beyond the fluff, that means the Avenger 4xe Hybrid Edition X is a daily that also meets the demands of users who prioritize styling, comfort, and the adventure-oriented lifestyle.
The visual treatment kicks off with surgically applied orange touches, beginning with orange for the seven-slot grille and orange X signature badging. The rest of the recipe is a black roof laid over two paint options, namely Stone and Concrete Grey. The manufacturer's Japanese subsidiary has confirmed 85 units apiece.
Stone is an earthy tone pitched as being a sophisticated color in the urban jungle yet visible off the beaten path, while Concrete Grey is a more self-explanatory color. Inside, customers are presented with black leather seats, power adjustments for the driver's seat, and heating for both front seats.
Underneath all of that, you will find the 4xe Hybrid powertrain the Japanese-market Avenger received back in March 2026. Said electrified setup pairs a 1.2-liter turbocharged inline-four gasser developed by French colossus Groupe PSA with a 48-volt system that feeds two electric motors. One handles the rear axle, which isn't connected to the tranny by a prop shaft.
Photo: Jeep This electric 4x4 solution is especially interesting when the fronts experience wheel slip, for electric drive also means near-instant torque delivery. Both electric motors develop 28 horsepower, with the front unit integrated into the six-speed transmission. All told, Stellantis Japan promises 145 ps (143 hp) and 230 Nm (170 lb-ft) at full chatter from the all-wheel-drive crossover.
In optimal conditions, the small crossover needs 9.5 seconds to hit 100 kilometers per hour (62 miles per hour). Despite being a 48-volt system, the Avenger 4xe Hybrid Edition X can be driven in full-electric mode at low speeds. Unfortunately, just like the rest of the range, the special edition also carries a 350,000-yen economic fluctuation surcharge that Stellantis Japan introduced earlier this year.
The company is citing the weak yen and rising manufacturing and logistics costs. The 350,000-yen surcharge applies to compact and urban models, while Jeep Wrangler customers have to spend 400,000 yen. All economic fluctuation surcharges are baked into the suggested retail price.
Originally priced at 4.99 million yen, the Avenger 4xe Hybrid for Japan currently retails at 5.19 million yen. That's 32,795 dollars at current exchange rates, while the special edition is roughly 33,105 freedom eagles.

Harley-Davidson Black Reaper Is Here to Snuff Out the Shine of the Low Rider ST
54 photos
Photo: Thunderbike
People’s taste in motorcycles is just as varied as people themselves, but if you really think about it, riders are part of two major categories: they either like their bikes chrome and shiny, or monochrome and, if possible, matte. This here story is (kind of) for those in the latter category.
Bike makers, including Harley-Davidson, know this, and that’s why most of the time they try their best to satisfy both tastes. They can’t help but show what kind of bodywork they prefer, though, and that’s why they generally lean to promote in a more obvious fashion one or the other.
Take the present-day Low Rider ST , which is offered in two trim levels, chrome and black, with four associated colors. No matter the choice, the Low Rider shows shiny elements in various quantities.
All the shine Harley includes on this bike from the factory floor has been completely snuffed out on the Black Reaper custom Low Rider ST we have here. Look all you want, and, with the exception of the fork legs, you won’t see a single trace of shiny chrome or any other metal.
The all-black club-styler, as German shop Thunderbike, its maker, calls it, is meant to send across a message of performance and unforgiveness. And if you ask me, it manages to do just that, even if, technically speaking, the Softail frame and Milwaukee-Eight engine are the same as they were when the bike rolled off the lines.
The bagger has been at the receiving end of the usual customization choices, starting with the fitting of new wheels and Brembo braking hardware and ending with the Dr. Jekill & Mr. Hyde silencers pulled over the exhaust system.
Having also modified the bike’s suspension system, Thunderbike was careful enough to make the motorcycle black in its entirety, and to gift it with only the tiniest touches of red for contrast and a more impressive appearance.
Everywhere you look, the changes made jump out to take you by surprise: the red brake caliper at the rear from under the swingarm, the original handlebars from where they have been relocated, and the Saddlemen step-up seat from high up on the frame.
At the front, the two-wheeler displays a Klock Werks windscreen, satin grips, and aftermarket turn signals, which at the front are hidden under the distinctive ST fairing. An impressive touch is the removal of the factory footpegs and the fitting of mini footboards in their place. This choice was made as a means to make long rides as comfortable as possible for the rider.
Not including the mechanical upgrades, such as they are, and the paint job, Thunderbike used some 20 custom parts from its inventory. Combined, they amount to $5,600, and that should give you a pretty decent idea of how much the project is worth.

Two Massachusetts cranberry bogs that had stopped making financial sense to farm are growing berries again – with solar panels overhead helping pay the bills.
The Black Cat project in Plymouth and the Ring Road project in Kingston combine cranberry farming, community solar, and battery storage. Distributed Energy Infrastructure (DEI), which built the projects, says income from leasing the land for solar has made it viable to cultivate the long-idle bogs again.
It’s a particularly challenging form of agrivoltaics because cranberry bogs have soft, peaty soil and established vines that need to survive construction. You can’t just roll in with heavy equipment and start installing panels.
So the solar had to fit the farming. In a September article in North American Clean Energy , DEI cofounder and executive vice president Prateek Tare described panels raised 10 feet above the ground, leaving room for farm machinery underneath. Rows have more than 18 feet of clear space between them, and solar panel angles let sunlight reach the cranberry bogs.

Farmer Iain Ward helped work out those details, along with how construction could proceed without damaging the bogs. Even the protective mats needed changing: Black ones absorbed too much heat, so crews used white ones instead.
That care added time. Tare said construction took around eight months – roughly twice as long as a comparable conventional solar project.
“The DEI team was phenomenal at understanding and adapting solar construction so that energy production could coexist without damage to the perennial cropping system,” Ward said.
Greenbacker Renewables owns both sites. Black Cat pairs 1 megawatt (MW) of solar with 2.7 megawatt-hours (MWh) of battery storage, while Ring Road has 4.4 MW of solar and a 13.5 MWh battery.
The money reaches both sides of the farming arrangement, too. The landowner receives solar land lease income, and Ward is paid to manage the bogs, in addition to his earnings from selling the berries.
DEI’s October announcement celebrates what it calls the first-ever agrivoltaic cranberry harvests, which Tare’s earlier account dates to fall 2025.

Kia launched a first-of-its-kind remote car-sharing program in Korea using the PV5 electric van.
Kia is using the PV5 EV van for remote car-sharing
The pilot program began operations on Thursday in Pangyo, Gyeonggi Province, using the Kia PV5, and it will run until the end of the year.
Kia said the new car-sharing service is the first of its kind in South Korea to use remote driving technology.
How does it work? Those interested can reserve a vehicle through a dedicated app. Once reserved, Kia’s electric van will drive itself to the requested location without a driver, using remote driving technology.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Users can drive the PV5 as they please and then park it at a desired location when they are finished. A remote driver will then move the vehicle back to its garage using 4G or 5G wireless technology.
Kia said the program can help businesses improve efficiency and reduce the burden of owning a fleet of vehicles. It’s also convenient to pick up and drop off the vehicle as you please.
A remote driver operating the PV5 remotely (Source: Kia)
The PV5 remote car-sharing pilot program is the latest in Kia’s push to advance remote driving technology.
Last April, Kia received a special exemption for the remote driving regulatory sandbox from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. In November 2025, it formed a Remote Driving Consortium with Socar, KT, and autonomous driving startup SUM, showcasing Korea’s First Remote Driving Demonstration on public roads by a domestic brand.
Most recently, Kia signed an MOU with KT and SUM in July to promote the commercialization of remote driving tech and aims to launch the service within a year.
Kia launches Korea’s first remote car-sharing using the PV5 (Source: Kia)
For the pilot service that launched this week, Kia, SUM, Mobiops, and the Korea Road Traffic Authority are participating in a consortium. Gyeonggi Province, KT, UMOS ONE, the Next Generation Convergence Technology Research Institute, and the Gyeonggi Automobile Rental Business Association are supporting the project as partner organizations.
Kia will provide PV5 vans and oversee the project. SUM will develop the remote driving solution, while Mobiops will handle service operations. Meanwhile, the Korea Road Traffic Authority assists with regulatory reviews.
During the pilot period, the partners will verify the remote driving technology and the feasibility of service operations under real-world conditions.
Using the data gathered during the trial, Kia plans to continue advancing the technology and expand the service in 2027 to accelerate the commercialization of PV5-based remote driving services.

Two laser weapons developed by Hanwha Systems shot down all three target drones during a South Korean Army demonstration on Oct. 14, the company said, as it pitches the technology to foreign buyers.
The company’s stationary Cheongwang laser air defense weapon and a 30-kilowatt-class vehicle-mounted laser took part in the live-fire event, held during the Army’s TIGER+ Future Warfare Integrated Combat Exercise. About 500 people attended, according to Hanwha, including Army Chief of Staff Gen. Kim Kyu-ha.
Cheongwang fired on a drone overhead that “caught fire and fell from the sky,” The Korea Times reported from the exercise at a training ground in Yangpyeong, Gyeonggi Province. The laser was one part of a layered counter-drone demonstration that also included electronic jamming and a K21 armored vehicle firing on incoming drones.
Hanwha did not say which system destroyed which drones, what kinds of drones were used, what vehicle carries the newer laser or the range of either weapon.
The Oct. 14 demonstration followed a Sept. 16 event at South Korea’s 2026 Defense Drone Technology Exhibition, where Cheongwang downed four drones and two larger unmanned aircraft in succession, Hanwha said.
Cheongwang, meaning “light of the sky,” in Korean is formally known as the Laser Air Defense Weapon Block-I. Hanwha developed it under a program led by South Korea’s Agency for Defense Development. The company calls it the world’s first operationally deployed laser weapon.
South Korea first fielded the system in December 2024 and had about five units at major government facilities as of June, including the Ministry of National Defense building, according to Korea JoongAng Daily .
North Korean drones have repeatedly violated South Korean airspace. In December 2022, five crossed the border, one reaching Seoul. Fighter jets, attack helicopters and warning shots failed to bring any of them down, Defense News reported at the time.
Hanwha says each Cheongwang shot costs about $1.50, in line with the figure South Korea’s arms procurement agency gave in 2024 . Unlike guns or missiles, the system uses no ammunition and can continue firing as long as it has power. The company asserts lasers can counter cheap drones used for surveillance and strikes without relying on much costlier missile-based air defenses.
Hanwha is also developing a 50 kW Laser Armored Vehicle in-house for export customers and displayed a model of it at the MSPO defense show in Kielce, Poland, in September.
At the show, Hanwha Systems manager Hyungun Park told Defense News that the company had built a prototype and planned to begin production by the end of 2027. He said Hanwha was in talks with potential buyers in Europe, Asia and the Middle East about exporting Cheongwang.
South Korea’s 2027 defense budget proposal includes funding to begin research on a mobile Block-II version of Cheongwang, UPI reported .

Michael Scanlon is a defense journalist covering air and space warfare. A former U.S. Air Force A-10 crew chief, he has supported land and sea programs for the U.S. Army, Navy, Marine Corps and Coast Guard.

The XM30 Combat Vehicle will serve as the U.S. Army’s infantry fighting vehicle to create an advantageous position and deliver a decisive strike, while also controlling maneuver robotics and semi-autonomous systems. (US Army photo by Aliyah Harrison)
WASHINGTON — The Army will make open systems architecture a key criterion when selecting the winner for its XM30 Optionally Manned Fighting Vehicle , a top official overseeing ground vehicles told Breaking Defense this week.
During an interview at the annual AUSA conference, Brig. Gen. Troy Denomy, portfolio acquisition executive for ground maneuver, said the Army is prioritizing the ability to rapidly adapt its platforms and integrate new technologies as threats evolve — particularly in the counter-unmanned aerial aerial systems fight.
“There’s other aspects that we are absolutely evaluating, but that one is hyper important to me, and we are actually going to evaluate that as part of this selection process, ” Denomy add ed.
The XM30 is intended to replace the Army’s Bradley Fighting Vehicle, which has served as a central component of the service’s armored formations for decades. The next-generation vehicle is being designed to give soldiers improved protection and capabilities to operate against new battlefield threats.
An open systems architecture allows the Army and its industry partners to plug new and different software and hardware capabilities into the platform as emerging tech becomes available and as the threat picture changes, Denomy explained. Out of the two vendors who are competing for the program — American Rheinmetall and General Dynamics Land Systems (GDLS) — he said it’s “too early to te ll” which company has implemented a more open architecture.
Both vendors have delivered one XM30 prototype each to the Army for testing at Aberdeen Proving Ground, Denomy said. Testing has identified some software capabilities that the vendors need to “tweak,” particularly involving communication between platform subsystems, he said.
“Both vendors are being very responsive to those changes that are necessary,” Denomy said. He added that “it’s nothing atypical for a prototype,” and the open systems architectures for both platforms have allowed the changes to be made quickly.
Though the government is operating under a continuing resolution and Congress has yet to pass the fiscal 2027 budget, Denomy told Breaking Defense that he believes the XM30 program will successfully move forward. He pointed to conversations the service had with congressional staff members at the Army Modernization Days in Aberdeen two weeks ago.
“We spent the whole day with the professional staff members and felt like what we were talking about was positively received of where we are in the program, and that we will be ready based off of our plan to execute the dollars with the appropriation forthcoming,” Denomy said.
The Army requested $547 million to procure 19 XM30s i n FY27, as Breaking Defense previously reported . However, the House Appropriations defense subcommittee drafted a version of th e FY27 s pending bill that reduced the procurement line to just $33.1 million.
Separately, Denomy said that the Army is conducting experimental testing with BAE Systems’ Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicle (AMPV) equipped with a 30mm Kongsberg turret — a platform known as the AMPV-30. The vehicle is c urrently “being exercised in an infantry fighting vehicle role” as part of a Transformation in Contact rotation, he said.
He said there are “significant differences between” what the AMPV-30 and XM30 can do and cautioned against conflating the two vehicles .
The AMPV-30 gives the Army an opportunity to explore an infantry fighting vehicle role for the platform, originally designed as a replacement for the M113 family of armored personnel carriers and support vehicles. Unlike the XM30, which is an Army-funded program, the AMPV-30 is self-funded by BAE Systems. Denomy praised BAE for investing its own funding to give the Army additional options, saying the effort could allow the AMPV to conduct more types of missions.
“For me what this showcases from an AMPV perspectiv e [are] potential opportunities in the future for other mission roles for it. They do the standard things that are part of the program of record — whether it’s the general purpose, the medical variant [or] the mission command variant. Well, now they’ve demonstrated [a version] with a turret that could fill a role,” he added.
Further, he emphasized that the “commitment behind XM30 is real and it’s important, and we have two very viable offerings.”

Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 16, 2026
Vizsla Copper (TSXV: VCU; US-OTC: VCUFF) plans to move its Palmer copper-zinc project in Alaska toward prefeasibility over the next two to three years, while keeping proposed acquisitions as longer-term upside, Senior Vice-President for Alaska Peter Mercer says.
The company’s 40,000-metre drilling program across Alaska and British Columbia is its largest yet. At Palmer , near Haines in southeast Alaska, the team is testing whether geological controls behind a high-grade copper core can help it find richer zones elsewhere on the property.
“Not all projects have to be advanced at the same time,” Mercer told The Northern Miner last month at the Precious Metals Summit in Beaver Creek, Colo. “We’ve got a great cash position right now, but it’s really going into next year, what provides that value for shareholders and how we can translate that through the drill bit.”
The project sequencing would let Vizsla use its Alaska team across a growing portfolio. Its proposed acquisition of Delta and Helm Bay from Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX, NYSE: AEM) would add two projects and make Canada’s biggest gold producer a major shareholder of Vizsla.

Montage Gold (TSX: MAU; US-OTC: MAUTF) is targeting higher-grade satellite deposits to boost output at its Koné mine in Côte d’Ivoire, CEO Martino De Ciccio says.
Koné, about 350 km northwest of the country’s capital, Yamoussoukro, poured its first gold late last month, after this interview was recorded. Montage expects its oxide processing circuit to reach commercial production by year-end, the company said in a subsequent update.
“It’s quite rare to be able to explore while building,” De Ciccio told The Northern Miner . “So for us, a key value driver is and will continue to be exploration.”
Montage has identified 12 deposits at Koné, compared with two included in its 2024 feasibility study, which projected average annual production exceeding 300,000 oz. over the first eight years. United Parcel Service’s new air hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines is 15 times larger than its predecessor, enabling the express carrier to provide up to two days faster delivery for customers within Asia and improve connectivity across its global network.
UPS ( NYSE: UPS ) spent $80 million on the expansion project, which includes specialized handling areas for healthcare, high-tech and manufacturing customers with time-sensitive and temperature-sensitive shipments. Parcel handling capacity increased to an average daily volume of 46,000, with maximum processing capacity of 15,000 pieces per hour, according to a news release on Thursday.
The announcement marks the first time UPS has disclosed the size of the capital expenditure to expand its Clark hub, which now covers 323,000 square feet.
UPS now operates 170 flight segments into and out of Clark every week, connecting businesses across Asia Pacific, India, Europe and the United States in as little as one business day. The new hub has also created nearly 600 jobs, the company said.
In August, the U.S. Department of Transportation approved the transfer of six UPS flying rights between Hong Kong and Warsaw, Poland, and Hanoi, Vietnam, to Clark Airport to support growing trade flows between the Philippines and Hong Kong.
UPS began operations at Clark, a former U.S. Air Force base, in 2002 and announced plans to build a new facility in March 2024.
Why It Matters: Service enhancements enabled by the new Clark hub include up to two days faster delivery to and from eastern China and other major Asia Pacific markets, and similar transit improvements between several Southeast Asian markets and India, UPS said. Faster service also enables UPS to extend shipment pickup windows at customer locations and make faster deliveries to cities in the region.
“Asia Pacific has been the heartbeat of global trade for years. There are still plenty of growth opportunities for the region’s businesses and a lot of untapped potential. Clark is the latest in a series of recent major investments UPS has made in its Asia Pacific network and there’s more to come as we continue to speed up connectivity, unlock trade growth opportunities, improve service reliability and strengthen supply chains for our customers,” said Bernard Jiang, president UPS Asia Pacific, in the news release.

1969 Ford Cobra Has the Great Original Ram Air 428 and Low Price, No One Cares It's a 1-of-1
12 photos
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Dale Baliles
Have we really reached the point where a genuine, factory-documented 1969 Ford Cobra with its matching-numbers 428 Cobra Jet V8 can sit on the market for two weeks without someone snatching it up? That is the exact scenario unfolding right now in Winchester, Virginia, where a seller has listed an original R-code fastback on a flatbed trailer for $22,500 or best offer, complete with a clean title and a bonus parts car.
To be fair, the 99,999 miles shown in the listing is just an online placeholder, and nobody is pretending this Blue Oval bruiser is ready for the local cruise night tonight. Still, the bones are mouthwatering for any blue-blooded gearhead: a factory R-code 428 Cobra Jet Ram Air engine paired with a 4-speed manual transmission, a tough 3.50:1 nodular-iron Traction-Lok rear axle, power steering, and power front disc brakes.
There are a few names in the car-verse that have the gravitas of a neutron star (only the densest cosmic object known to science, after the zero-volume-infinite-density black hole mind-wrecker), and Cobra Jet is one of those heavyweights. The legendary Ford motor is probably most associated with Mustangs – for some reason, people tend to forget about the Blue Oval’s mid-size killer, the Cobra.
This is probably one of history’s most offensive injustices, since the 1969 Ford Fairlane Torino Talladega won 29 races in NASCAR. Ironically, the aerodynamic Talladega didn’t win the inaugural Talladega 500 race, where the Dodge Charger Daytona debuted. The controversy looms to this day whether Ma Mopar sweet-talked Bill France, the boss of NASCAR, into pulling some strings to puppeteer the Chrysler onto the highest step of the podium for a perfect introduction of the new model.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Dale Baliles No matter what happened on the track that day, the 1969 championship went to Ford. On the street, however, the dispute was much heated, with Dodge’s Charger R/T and Ford’s Cobra taking turns at punching each other with every stoplight opportunity they got. Eventually, the Mopar got the upper hand, selling nearly 4,500 more cars than the FoMoCo muscle car (19,298 versus 14,885).
The big irony of it was that the Cobra didn’t get the Boss 429 engine, which was also launched in 1969 specifically for NASCAR homologation. Picture this: the NASCAR car didn’t get the NASCAR engine on the street. The Mustang Boss 429 did – which wasn’t running it in NASCAR. The Ford Cobra ran with the 428 Cobra Jet for civilian use. It was the only engine offered in the bare-bones muscle car, but it could be optioned with the Ram Air function, for 113 extra bucks.
Now back to the car in this story – and gallery. A closer look at it strapped onto its trailer reveals why it takes a brave soul with a well-equipped garage to step up. Its factory Indian Fire red paint has faded into a chalky, sun-baked patina, and both the front windshield and the sweeping fastback rear glass are completely gone. There is a noticeable dent in the driver's door, and the rear bumper wears plenty of surface rust.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Dale Baliles Despite the rough edges, the overall body lines look remarkably straight, the quad-headlight grille and front bumper are intact, and the hooded scoop with its factory hold-down pins still commands respect. The car currently sits on aftermarket 5-slot mag wheels rather than its original 14-inch Argent styled steel wheels. Inside, a thick coat of dust covers the four-pod instrument cluster, the factory tachometer, and the original three-spoke steering wheel.
Piled with a silver tarp and a blanket, the cabin still retains its black vinyl bucket seats, even if the passenger cushion has a split seam, alongside the center console and 4-speed shifter. Under the cut-out hood sits the matching-numbers 428 V8 wearing finned aluminum valve covers and an aftermarket open-element air cleaner. Better yet, the deal includes a 1969 Torino GT 302 automatic parts car with intact glass.
Understanding why a project like this matters requires looking back at the muscle car wars of the late 1960s. When Plymouth shook up the industry in 1968 with the stripped-down, budget-priced Road Runner street bruiser, Dodge quickly followed with the Super Bee, while Pontiac prepared its brash GTO Judge for 1969. Buyers clearly wanted maximum horsepower in an intermediate body without paying extra money for plush interior trim and heavy luxury add-ons.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Dale Baliles Ford answered that call in 1969 by borrowing the iconic Cobra name it had acquired from Carroll Shelby and slapping it onto a stripped-down Fairlane intermediate chassis. Marketed simply as the Cobra, without Fairlane or Torino sobriquets, this one-year-only model came in two body styles: a formal two-door hardtop with a $3,206 base price and a sleek two-door SportsRoof fastback starting at $3,189, undercutting fancier rivals while putting every single dollar into pure street performance.
Every 1969 Cobra left the factory with serious firepower under the hood. The base powerplant was the Q-code 428-cubic-inch four-barrel Cobra Jet V8 without functional hood induction, while stepping up to the optional R-code 428-cubic-inch Cobra Jet Ram Air V8 added a functional scoop that force-fed cool air into the carburetor. A heavy-duty 4-speed manual transmission was standard equipment, and a rugged 3-speed SelectShift Cruise-O-Matic automatic transmission was also optional.
Fitted with 10.6:1 compression and a 735-cfm Holley carburetor, both the Q-code and R-code 428 engines were conservatively rated at 335 horsepower at 5,200 rpm and 440 lb-ft of torque at 3,400 rpm. Ordering a 3.91:1 or 4.30:1 rear axle brought Super Cobra Jet internals. Period tests clocked the Cobra from 0 to 60 mph in 7.3 seconds and through the quarter-mile in 14.9 seconds at 95.2 mph, with tops speeds in the vicinity of 125 mph.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace/Dale Baliles Despite that blistering pace, overall 1969 Cobra production remained relatively modest, split between 3,786 hardtops and 11,099 fastbacks. According to the Marti Report included with this Winchester car, this Indian Fire example was ordered on September 6, 1968, and built at the Lorain, Ohio plant on November 12, 1968, running 35 days behind schedule before selling at Bristol Ford in Pennsylvania on February 19, 1969.
That same Marti Report breaks down just how special this particular SportsRoof truly is. Out of all the 1969 Cobra SportsRoofs built, 7,454 had the R-code 428 Cobra Jet Ram Air, with 3,910 of them carrying a close-ratio 4-speed manual transmission. The numbers drop abruptly after that: only 175 put on the Indian Fire war paint and the black vinyl bucket seats.
If we really want to nitpick the numbers, we can – this is a one-of-one, if we account for the white sidewalls, Argent steelies, and remote-controlled left mirror. But that’s just like saying it’s the only one built by a man named Joe wearing a red hat and a goatee and size 8 shoes.
Let’s keep it real. It’s a rare muscle car, it still has the numbers-matching big-block, and it takes plenty of elbow grease to bring back. Well, that, and $22,500 (with the donor Torino included) – a number that, for some reason, seems to fend off buyers. But why?

The order to limit a satellite system used by Ukraine for battlefield communications and drone operations came from inside the White House, according to two U.S. officials and a Western official briefed on the matter.
The officials said leaders at the Defense Department received a message that the SpaceX Starshield service for the Ukrainian military needed to be slowed.
The officials, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, did not specify who in the White House made the decision or who was responsible for implementing the order. The Pentagon is the biggest customer of Starshield, which is the military-grade version of the Starlink service.
Ukrainian officials said this week that military-grade Starlink receptors stopped working in Ukraine when mounted on fast-moving objects, interfering with the performance of ‌Ukrainian drones that rely on them for onboard guidance systems over Ukrainian territory.
A person in Ukraine’s Defence Ministry said on Thursday that the receptors were now working when in motion, but only at speeds of up to 100 miles per hour (160 kph).
U.S. pressures Ukraine over refinery attacks
The move to temporarily restrict the vital communications system came as President Donald Trump has pressured Kyiv to stop its attacks on Russian refineries, which he has blamed for the soaring energy prices that are denting his Republican Party’s prospects in the November midterm elections.
But experts say that surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, which brought Iranian attacks on energy facilities and has largely shut the vital Strait of Hormuz.
In response to a request for comment about the order to limit Starshield, a senior U.S. official said: “No such request was ever made by the president.”
The White House did not respond to questions about whether other administration officials might have made the request.
Starshield was developed by SpaceX specifically for government and national-security customers, particularly the U.S. Department of Defense. Starshield uses the Starlink constellation as its backbone.
Ukrainian officials said the restrictions complicated strike missions against Russian forces and logistics in occupied territory and slowed interceptor drones used to shoot down incoming Russian Shahed drones.
Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX, said on X on Wednesday that because Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government, any limits on speed or usage are decided by the U.S. military or the president.
SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment.
The Department of Defense and the Ukrainian embassy in Washington also did not respond to requests for comment.
Decline in relations
Relations between Kyiv and Washington have deteriorated in recent days following a meeting in Miami on Oct. 9 that convened representatives from both countries as well as Europe and the World Bank.
Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, the Trump administration’s Middle East envoy, struck a tough tone with Ukraine in the meeting, according to a separate person familiar with the matter. They told Ukrainian officials that the U.S. was frustrated with Kyiv’s continued strikes on Russian refineries despite repeated requests from Washington to stop.
The U.S. delegation also explained Washington’s decision to strike a diesel deal with Russia, saying the White House hoped it would soften Moscow’s stance on peace talks.
That deal, under which Russia will supply more than 2.25 million barrels of diesel to ​U.S. and global markets, has triggered a backlash from some U.S. lawmakers, who say it will give Moscow cash to pursue its war without forcing Russian President Vladimir Putin to make concessions to end the conflict.
In the days that followed, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Trump criticized each other, with Zelenskiy calling the U.S. decision on the Russian diesel deal “weak.” Trump called for elections in Ukraine and Zelenskiy’s ouster.
Behind the scenes, American officials threatened to stop providing intelligence to Kyiv about Russian missile launches that Ukraine uses to thwart attacks, as Reuters previously reported. Trump said on Tuesday Washington was still sharing intelligence with Ukraine.
Following the move to restrict Ukraine’s access to Starshield, the Ukrainians made calls on Tuesday and Wednesday to find answers from senior officials at the White House, State Department and Pentagon, a senior Ukrainian official said, adding that Kyiv was told it was a White House decision.
The Pentagon has spent billions of dollars on the Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft ​for missile-warning missions and a spy ​constellation for the National Reconnaissance ⁠Office, Reuters reported in 2024.

source_document.body:
Container shipping is facing an escalating threat in the Strait of Hormuz, which can impact shippers far from the region.
The attacks this week included the Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, which caught fire and sank with containers still aboard.
Maritime authorities reported at least 10 vessels attacked in or near the chokepoint since Sunday, with six incidents on Sunday alone, the highest one-day total since the U.S.-Iran war began in February.
The 2,824-TEU feeder vessel GFS Pride was hit by an unknown projectile on Tuesday while transiting the strait, sustaining damage and a fire before sinking off Oman. Singapore’s Maritime and Port Authority said all 21 crew members were evacuated safely and no injuries were reported.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said the vessel struck a naval mine on an “unauthorized” route and was carrying contraband. Singaporean authorities and maritime analysts disputed that account, with the MPA saying the ship was struck by projectiles; CNN reported that experts assessed a drone strike as the more likely cause.
A second Singapore-flagged container ship, the GFS Giselle, was also struck by projectiles and suffered hull damage, but reached safe anchorage under its own power; its 22 crew members were reported safe.
Two other feeder vessels were also hit, including the 2,500-TEU DP World Kaveri operated by a unit of Dubai’s DP World.
The downstream effect can resonate far beyond attacks in the region.
Other carriers may have bought feeder slots on the vessels, suggested analyst Lars Jensen. He noted Maersk (OTC: AMKBY ), Ocean Network Express, PIL and OOCL showed active schedules for some of the ships.
Analysts point out that for shippers, war insurance can be cancelled on short notice if cargo moves on a vessel not owned by the carrier listed on the bill of lading .
British security monitor UKMTO data showed 12 vessels reported attacks between Oct. 5 and Oct. 11, the largest weekly total since the war began, following 10 attacks the prior week. Six vessels were struck on Sunday, including five tankers and one container ship.
The GFS Pride and the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao, which sank after being struck on Sept. 23, are the second and third vessels to sink since the conflict began, according to IMO casualty data.
Iran has linked the intensified campaign to the U.S. blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions, while U.S. Central Command said commercial traffic continues through the strait with coordinated protection from American forces and regional partners.
The violence is beginning to constrain traffic. Analyst Kpler counted 131 crossings through the strait in the week ended Oct. 14, down from 176 the previous week, though the firm cautioned that the decline was not solely attributable to the latest attacks.
Kpler estimated 12.6 million barrels of crude oil per day moved through the strait on Oct. 13, below the roughly 15 million barrels per day reported at the end of September.

Bulgaria has formally asked NATO to deploy combat aircraft and anti-drone systems to bolster its defenses after a series of drone attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea, Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov said on Friday.
Drones hit two ships that caught fire off Romania’s Black Sea coast this week. On Tuesday, a commercial vessel sank off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast following a drone attack, prompting Sofia to summon Russia’s ambassador.
The attacks have highlighted the growing threat that drone warfare linked to the Russia-Ukraine conflict poses to commercial shipping near NATO’s southeastern flank, prompting Bulgaria to push for stronger alliance defenses in the Black Sea.
“We have sent letters and a request to the NATO Secretary General and the Supreme Allied Commander, urging them to strengthen our capabilities, which also means deploying additional forces on our territory. We are awaiting their decision,” Stoyanov said.
Stoyanov said he planned to meet his Romanian and Turkish counterparts soon to discuss coordinating action and a common approach to the situation in the Black Sea.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev and Romanian President Nicusor Dan on Thursday, saying afterwards that NATO would “continue to work closely with our Allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed.”
Asked about Bulgaria’s request on Friday, a NATO official said the issue would be discussed further by ambassadors from the alliance’s 32 member states next week.
Bulgaria, which has proposed a moratorium on attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea, also expects to join a NATO anti-drone initiative by the end of October.

2027 Lexus TX Bids Farewell to 550h+ PHEV, Rest of the Range Gets Upgraded
62 photos
Photo: Lexus
The battle for supremacy in the mid-size luxury crossover segment is as fierce as ever, and, to be able to wage it, the players doing business there have to constantly offer something new. I’m not entirely sure how the (relatively minor) changes announced by Lexus for its 2027 TX can help with that, but here they are nonetheless.
Launched three years ago and presently in its first generation, the SUV built on the same Global Architecture-K (GA-K) platform that underpins the Toyota Grand Highlander and the Lexus RX and NX soldiers on into the new model year in seven trim levels, packing a choice of two powertrains, and one model poorer.
The biggest news for the year must be the removal from the lineup of the TX 550h+ plug-in hybrid (PHEV) for undisclosed reasons that probably have to do with less than optimal sales. Nothing comes in its place, at least for now.
The seven trim levels that will be available from now on for this SUV include both standard and F Sport models. They are Standard, Premium, Luxury, F Sport Handling, F Sport Performance Premium, and F Sport Performance Luxury. They can be had with either the gasoline powertrain known as the TX 350, or with the TX 500h hybrid electric setup.
The TX 350 is the engine of choice for the Standard, Premium, F Sport Handling, and Luxury trim levels. It consists of the 2.4-liter turbocharged inline-four engine that’s also deployed on the RX and NX, and in this application is rated at 275 horsepower and 317 lb.-ft. of torque.
Photo: Lexus The engine can send its power to either the front wheels or all four of them, in carefully controlled bursts with the help of the close-ratio eight-speed direct shift automatic transmission.
The top-of-the-range TX 500h is only available in an all-wheel drive configuration on the F Sport Performance models, and it combines a 2.4-liter turbocharged engine with a six-speed automatic transmission, an integrated power control unit, a 64-kW electric motor, and a 76-kW eAxle at the rear.
This setup is good for 366 hp and 406 lb.-ft. of torque, and, to get it going, the TX 500h also uses a nickel-metal hydride (NiMH) battery installed beneath the second row of seats.
When it comes to the upgrades made to the range, Lexus itself describes them as minor. On the 350, the Japanese carmaker made changes to the vacuum brake booster and brake hold feature, and gave the 20-inch aluminum wheels that make the connection to the ground a darker gray finish.
Photo: Lexus The non-F Sport models also get a new color, or, should I say, an expanding color. That would be the Matador Red Mica that is already available on the Sport SUVs.
In terms of the suspension system chosen to underpin the TX, Lexus went for a MacPherson strut at the front and a five-arm multi-link at the rear. A standard rack assist-type electric power steering is on deck to take the TX where it needs to go, backed by a dynamic rear steering system on the F Sport Performance.
On a visual level, Lexus did not change all that much to help the 2027 TX advance on people’s minds and bank accounts, but it did modify a bit the front fascia both for effect and to leave room for the front spindle to regulate airflow while cooling the brakes.
There are a total of seven colors offered on the TX for the 2027 model year, none of them new to the range. Wheel choices range from 20 inches to 22 inches, depending on the trim level chosen.
Photo: Lexus Lexus did nothing to better the interior of the LX SUV, but that’s probably because it didn’t need to. All versions continue to offer, thus, a 12.3-inch multi-information display behind the steering wheel and a 14-inch touchscreen front and center, captain’s chairs or a 60:40 split-folding bench in the rear, and a third row of seats that’s accessible by means of a walk-in mechanism.
The only worth mentioning things that were added for the new model year are the six modular cupholders that accompany the captain’s chairs. When the bench is selected, only four of them are on deck.
There are three interior color options for the 2027 Lexus TX, namely Peppercorn, Birch, and Black. The Blackwood trim ornamentation, made of ash wood with black woodgrain, is available across the range.
As it has always done, the new TX will be assembled for Lexus at the Toyota Motor Manufacturing facility in Indiana. The new version will sell starting at $58,890, including delivery, processing, and handling. The full list of prices for all models can be found below.
